subject: Audit logs: temporary retention waiver + proposed DPA amendment
messages:
From: Jorge Sanchez <j.sanchez@healthsync.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: dpo@healthsync.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: audit log retention waiver & subprocessor/transfer details

Hi Avery,

Quick note from HealthSync Legal/DPO — during our SOC2 audit planning we discovered that some of our clinical debugging workflows require access to server-side audit logs going back ~18 months. We understand Redwood's standard operational log retention is 90 days (and backups follow the same purge cadence), but for the purposes of incident reconstruction and regulatory obligations for a limited set of accounts we need an exception.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can provision a temporary retention waiver for audit logs tied to our tenant for 18 months?
- How backups are purged and what the timeline would be to remove historical copies if we later revert to standard retention?
- Whether any of the backups or logs for our tenant leave the US (we are particularly concerned about transfers to EU regions), and a current subprocessor list (we need to map to our vendor risk register).

We are under a compressed audit timeline and would appreciate a proposal by EOD Friday. If it helps, I can share a short formal justification memo (we have an internal legal requirement to retain certain audit trails for investigations).

Thanks,
Jorge
Jorge Sanchez
Head of Security Operations, HealthSync
[j.sanchez@healthsync.com]

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Cc: dpo@healthsync.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: audit log retention waiver & subprocessor/transfer details

Thanks Jorge — appreciate the heads up and the context. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (infra/ops) so we can give a concrete proposal. Quick responses up front:

- We can consider a tenant-scoped retention exception for logs/backups, but it will have guardrails (limited timeframe, explicit scope of log types, and extra cost to cover storage + egress risk).
- Backup purge: our standard backup lifecycle is cold snapshot -> 30d snapshot rotation -> 90d purge for indexable logs. For special exceptions we can create a retention slice where snapshots are pinned for the requested window, but we need an agreed purge procedure for any retained copies (including offsite/replicated copies).
- Data transfers: by default hosted tenants are routed to the US region; however automated replication to other regions can occur for DR. We'll need to confirm any EU-hosted replicas and provide a subprocessor export.

Action items we propose for Friday:
1) Kimberly to draft DPA amendment language that covers the exception, scope, and deletion playbook.
2) Karthik to export current subprocessor list + a short note on cross-region replication flags for HealthSync's tenant.
3) I will draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) outlining the timeframe and rollback triggers.

If you can share the justification memo that would help. For context, we'll attach our retention matrix and an initial draft amendment for your review.

Attachments: [Attachment: retention_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)]

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson

Subject: Draft: limited retention exception & DPA amendment (v0.1)

Hi Jorge / Avery,

Per the ask, I've put together draft amendment language and operational guardrails to enable an 18-month retention carveout for HealthSync. High-level summary follows, full draft attached.

Summary of proposed terms:
- Scope: Tenant-scoped audit logs and derived analytics artifacts used solely for incident reconstruction; does not include raw customer data stored in user-facing indexes.
- Duration: 18 months from effective date, with an automatic sunset unless HealthSync requests renewal in writing.
- Access controls: Retained artifacts will be placed in a segmented storage bucket with restricted access (security key escrow + audit trail of access).
- Purge/rollback: At end of the exception window we will run a coordinated purge that removes primary and replicated snapshots. The purge will include a validation report and a 72-hour window during which HealthSync can request hold or escalation.
- Data transfers: Redwood will certify no routine transfer of these retained artifacts to EU-based compute outside of documented DR replicas. Any DR replication to EU will be logged and consented in the amendment.
- Subprocessors: we will provide an export of current subprocessors and indicate which have access to retention-pinned storage.
- Fees: Fee schedule attached as Exhibit A; covers storage, additional audit logging, and ops support for purge coordination.

Next steps (proposed):
1) HealthSync to review v0.1 and confirm the specific log types and legal justification memo (we need explicit categories so we can scope storage tiers correctly).
2) Redwood infra to produce subprocessor_export_20261010.csv and a short note on replication flags (Karthik).
3) Legal to finalize DPA amendment and produce a DocuSign packet once we have confirmations.

I've attached: DPA_draft_amendment_v0.1.pdf (full proposed language) and a one-page fee exhibit.

Attachments: [Attachment: DPA_draft_amendment_v0.1.pdf (PDF, 72KB)]

Thanks,
